_note: Canonical backlog for Project Io — the authoritative METADATA index of every backlog item.
One item = one object in `items`.
STATUS (authoritative; JSON wins over any prose/glyph disagreement):
designed    (glyph ✓) — design settled, promote-ready.
design-owed (glyph ~) — design still owed; must be settled before promotion.
PRIORITY (ascending): F C B A S SSS.
F=deferred/parked, C=low, B=medium, A=important, S=high, SSS=do-immediately.
`parked:true` is the explicit flag for F-priority items.
DIFFICULTY (1-5): 1=~5min, 2=~20min, 3=~1h, 4=~3h, 5=~12h+ (break a 5 down).
SEQUENCING: `requires` lists BL-XXX ids of backlog items that must land first (supercedes the
old `waits_on` short_name list — v2 schema 2026-06-17). `blocked_on` names a truly-external
prerequisite with no backlog item (third-party dep, real-world gate). An item can be `designed`
and still have unmet `requires`. Both fields are nullable; [] means no dependencies.
WORKFLOW: a `designed` item is PROMOTED into REFINED.md and DELIVERED (see DELIVERY.md).
A `design-owed` item is DESIGNED first (prose settled in `design` field, status flipped).
When work lands, the item is RETAINED here under a terminal status (complete/shipped) with a
resolution/completion_note, and design propagates into the authority doc. (Convention updated
2026-07-04: terminal items were once removed; the tooling — gyre.py, progress counts — now
depends on them staying. Do not delete landed entries.)
DESIGN PROSE — the `design` field (policy updated 2026-06-17):
- ALL items: prose lives in the `design` field here, not in BACKLOG.md.
- NEW items: author prose here directly. No BACKLOG.md body.
- LEGACY items (pre-2026-06-17): `design: "@BACKLOG.md"` means prose is still in markdown.
Migrate to this field on first edit (design settle or promotion) — do not wait for promotion.
On migration: write prose here, replace the BACKLOG.md body with a tombstone line.
- ON PROMOTION into REFINED.md: delete any remaining BACKLOG.md body (if not yet migrated).
- BACKLOG.md therefore only drains, never grows, and is deleted once empty.
- For designs with rich tables use markdown in the `design` string (tables render fine).
- `design: "@<doc>"` is also valid as a pointer to an authority doc when prose lives there.
VERSION GOAL (policy added 2026-07-08): every NEW item names which version it is FOR via the
`version_goal` field — the minor it targets ("v0.0.9"), the next one ("v0.1.0"), or
"post-v0.1.0" for anything beyond the prototype's remaining arc (see ROADMAP.md for the
live version sequence and themes). This is a goal, not a promise — it may slip a version at
re-sequencing, same as priority. Legacy items predating this policy are not backfilled; treat
a missing `version_goal` as "unset (legacy)", not as "post-v0.1.0".

items.title: Placement-suitability surface (a lens on tile selection, not a strip lens)
items.summary: For a selected/armed building type, tint tiles by validity/affinity (valid highlighted, invalid greyed, thrives-here stronger). NOT an overlay_mode. Design owed: trigger, colour treatment, state model.
items.design:
**Explicitly *not* an `overlay_mode` strip lens** — a surface tied to **tile selection**: when the player selects a tile, every other tile is tinted by how well the selected tile's best valid building type would do there — a siting aid answering *where else could this kind of building go, and where is it best*. Reads the terrain enums and `src/world/placement_rules.hpp` already in place.

**Design settled (2026-06-16):** trigger is **tile selection only** (not armed-build mode). Colour treatment: **affine tiles** (terrain optimal for the building) receive a coloured tint; **invalid tiles** (building cannot be placed) receive a **dark overlay**; valid-but-not-affine tiles are **uncoloured** (no signal). Canvas-state model: the surface is tied to `selected_tile` state, not `overlay_mode` — it activates alongside the selection element and deactivates when nothing is selected. Authority `docs/ui/LENSES.md` (note the strip-lens distinction), `docs/economy/PRODUCTION.md`.

**Trigger revised (2026-06-30):** the 2026-06-16 *tile-selection* trigger was reversed — re-tinting the whole map on every inspection click read as a spurious lens change and fought the active strip lens. The surface is now gated on **construction mode** (`construction.active`) and keyed to the **armed** building type/target (not the selected tile's best building): a bare selection never re-skins the map, and the siting aid appears exactly while a build is armed. Affinity (the green thrives-here tint) applies to extraction only — a tile whose own richest extractable is the armed target. `src/ui/body_surface_canvas.cpp`.

items.title: Reach / Logistics-range lens
items.summary: Body-level reach lens: which bodies a corp's trade routes currently connect to, tiered by recency. Standalone lens, distinct from BL-014's flow read. Unblocked — BL-039/BL-088 landed.
items.design:
**Status:** complete. Landed 35dd1fb: `overlay_mode::reach` renders an on-canvas key/readout (connected-bodies list + recency tier) for the active body's own connections — `body_surface_canvas.cpp` only ever renders the active body's tile grid, so the originally-envisioned cross-body glow/marker rendering isn't reachable there; that fuller visual is a follow-up for `solar_system_canvas.cpp`. Dedicated icon glyph also deferred (reuses `icons::convoy`). Build clean; visual verification not yet run. Prior design: Unblocked: BL-039 (Supply convoys) and BL-088 (persistent `trade_route`) are both complete, so lane data exists at the body level. No distance-cost/falloff model exists anywhere in `supply_system`, so this scopes to what the data actually supports rather than inventing new physics.

**Shape (settled):** standalone lens — its own `overlay_mode::reach` and strip icon — not a Supply sub-mode. Reach reads *static coverage*; BL-014's Supply lens reads *live flow*; distinct enough to earn separate slots.

**Model.** For the selected corp, reach = the set of bodies connected via that corp's `trade_route` entries from a chosen origin body, tiered by `last_tick` recency — reuse the fresh/aging/stale tiering convention from the activity fog (`docs/ui/DISCOVERY.md`, BL-089) rather than inventing new thresholds. No physical falloff radius: a body is connected (with a recency tier) or it isn't — `trade_route` carries no distance/strength field to derive one from.

**Rendering.** Body-to-body highlight (glow/outline on the body marker) on the relevant canvas/minimap, not a per-tile field — reach is body-level connectivity, matching `trade_route`'s granularity.

Open at promotion: reuse DISCOVERY.md's exact stale-aging tick thresholds rather than picking new ones; confirm player-only vs all-corps rendering (competitor-visibility rule — likely player's own routes only). Authority docs/ui/LENSES.md; relates to BL-014.

items.title: Supply-routes lens — market-connection graph
items.summary: Graph of trade routes between bodies, edge thickness from convoy_count (volume proxy), recency-tiered colour. Aggregated from BL-088's trade_route list, not per-frame. Unblocked — BL-039/BL-088 landed.
items.design:
**Status:** complete. Landed 35dd1fb: `overlay_mode::supply_routes` renders an on-canvas key/readout of the active body's lanes (log-scaled thickness bar per lane + recency-tier colour) rather than cross-body edges, for the same body_surface_canvas.cpp scoping reason as BL-011; the fuller line-between-body-markers visual is a follow-up for `solar_system_canvas.cpp`. Build clean; visual verification not yet run. Prior design: Unblocked: BL-088 gives a persistent `trade_route` (`body_a`, `body_b`, `corp`, `last_tick`, `convoy_count`) per lane.

**Edge worth (scoped down).** `trade_route` carries no running $-value, so 'net trade worth' as originally framed isn't available without a new ledger. Settled: use `convoy_count` (cumulative completions) as the volume proxy for edge thickness, log-scaled so a few heavy lanes don't swamp the rest. Edge colour/alpha = recency tier from `last_tick`, sharing the fresh/aging/stale convention with BL-011 and the activity fog (DISCOVERY.md, BL-089).

**Aggregation (settled):** one edge per unordered (`body_a`, `body_b`) pair, built from the `trade_routes` list at render time — not per-frame convoy positions. Cheap and matches the lens's 'graph', not 'live traffic', framing.

**Rendering.** Line between body markers on the relevant canvas, thickness from log-scaled `convoy_count`, colour/alpha from recency tier.

Open at promotion: the log-scale constant (tune by eye); player-only vs all-corps lane rendering (competitor-visibility rule — likely player's own routes only, consistent with the activity fog). Authority docs/ui/LENSES.md; relates to BL-011.

items.design:
**Problem.** Tooltips give too much data. Reframe them: **less information, lens-specific**, aimed at explaining **why** a system behaves as it does — not at gathering data for quick decisions (that is the ledgers' job). The 2026-06-24 accessibility review adds a **cognitive-accessibility** rationale: the colour-coded lenses impose interpretive load, and a 'why, not what' tooltip that names what a lens is showing reduces that load (and pairs with the on-canvas labels/legend in BL-016).

**Defer nested tooltips.** Flagged as a **large, multi-round sweep** touching every visible entity — a sweep, not a single edit. Couples to the hover-card primitive (BL-060) and `docs/ui/TOOLTIP.md`.

**Open questions (design owed):** the per-entity, per-lens content sweep; the 'why' phrasing per lens; how it coordinates with the BL-016 legend so the two do not duplicate. The **cognitive half** of the accessibility strand. Authority `docs/ui/TOOLTIP.md`. *(Written 2026-06-16, v0.0.6 brief intake; cognitive-accessibility note 2026-06-24.)*

items.summary: Extend deposit authoring from the 7-resource subset to the full raw set via a seeded per-resource rarity scalar [0,1] (raw-tier only) modulating frequency/magnitude over terrain affinity. Scheduled to v0.2; data-only.
items.design:
**Scope: v0.2 (post-prototype) -- deferred, NOT implemented.** The prototype targets v0.1.0 (ROADMAP); full-set deposit authoring is outside the current arc, so per the standing scope rule it is not built now.

**Direction settled (2026-06-15); mechanics settle with the v0.2 tile-generation brief.** A **seeded per-resource rarity scalar** -- a decimal in [0, 1] (0 = trace/absent, 1 = near-universal ambient), **raw-tier resources only** (refined and product goods are made, not mined, so carry no deposits). The scalar **modulates deposit frequency and magnitude** on top of the existing terrain affinity, so a low scalar keeps a good sparse even on affine terrain and a high one approaches the every-tile ambient floor; it is **seeded** so a campaign's exact distribution varies while the rarity *ordering* (consistent with each good's RESOURCES.md base-price rarity) stays stable. The generation *mechanics* that consume the scalar are the tile-generation brief (BL-051), the same v0.2 pass. Settled into docs/economy/RESOURCES.md § Deposit rarity & scarcity and docs/generation/TILE_GENERATION.md § Deferred. Touches the deposit pass in src/world/tile_generation.cpp (data-only -- the deposit arrays already carry full enum width). src/-changing -> a headless deposit-distribution audit requirement at promotion. Status stays design-owed: direction is settled but the item is not promote-ready until the v0.2 pass is scheduled.

**Record note (2026-07-04 reconciliation).** The 2026-07-01 'pointer repaired' note was wrong -- a full BL-040 body *did* survive in BACKLOG.md (richer than the reconstruction it replaced). That body is folded in above and tombstoned in BACKLOG.md.

items.title: Habitability gates max workforce, not production directly
items.summary: Habitability caps a building's max workforce fraction (not output directly): >~0.6 -> 100% base; below, reduced. Tech later raises above 100% (0.99 -> ~250%). Design owed: the curve, the over-100% tech model.
items.design:
**Habitability should not scale a building's production output directly** — instead it caps the **building's max workforce fraction**. Couples to the contention scalar and the building workforce-target control; pairs with the Population/Opportunity lens (BL-017).

**Design settled (2026-06-16):** curve is **linear, stepped at 0.6** — habitability 0.0→0.6 maps linearly to 0%→100% max workforce fraction; at or above 0.6, max fraction is **100% base workforce**. Below 0.6 the fraction scales proportionally (e.g. hab 0.3 → 50% max). The tech-driven over-100% multiplier is **deferred** — settle the interface point when the research system lands. Authority `docs/economy/POPULATION.md`, `docs/SYSTEMS.md` § Workforce.

items.title: Generate the saturated nation-owned background substrate
items.summary: Per-tile substrate_density [0,1] on tile_component; nation_substrate aggregate (background supply+demand arrays) in world; population-ripple generation pass; economy tick injects substrate supply/demand into per-body markets. Static for v0.0.6. Continuous density model. Lens visual deferred to v0.2.
items.design:
Form: per-tile substrate_density float [0,1] on tile_component (nation-owned background productivity). Aggregated into a nation_substrate struct per (nation, body) in world — background_supply[resource_count] and background_demand[resource_count] arrays injected each economy tick into per-body market clearing. No per-building entities.

Generation — population sub-pass (settled 2026-06-16): co-generated with population centres (BL-036). Each tile substrate_density = max(0, 1 − distance_from_nearest_centre / ripple_radius) × centre_strength, where population centres are major clusters in the generation pass. Seeded inside nation_generation.cpp or a new substrate generation pass.

Dynamic growth model (settled 2026-06-17): STATIC for v0.0.6 — generated once at world-gen, no per-Tick evolution. Dynamic growth deferred to v0.2.

Slot/capacity model (settled 2026-06-17): CONTINUOUS density — substrate_density [0,1] = fraction of tile capacity used by background industry. Player buildings claim from (1 − density) headroom. Maps to integer-slot model (BL-043) when that lands.

Market coupling: on each economy tick, nation_substrate aggregate for (nation, body) contributes background_supply[r] and background_demand[r] to the body market clearing, scaled by nation territory tile count × mean density × per-resource terrain affinity factor. Gives markets real liquidity.

**Status:** designed — shape only (2026-07-08); still parked/out-of-scope, not promote-ready. Settling the structure now (per BL-087's model) so it's ready to pick up once nations move from generation-only to a system.

**Shape.** Four coupled parts, all deterministic and tick-driven like the rest of `world/*`:

1. **Nation SYSTEM.** A nation gets simple per-tick economic state — tax rate (levied on corp production/trade within its territory), a licence gate (a corp needs a licence to build/operate in a nation, cost scales with nation character), and a coarse infrastructure scalar (modulates production/logistics efficiency, generated once, degrading/improving slowly). War is a state flag between nation pairs affecting licence issuance and infrastructure decay, not a combat system — actual Conflict mechanics live elsewhere.
2. **Sentiment graph.** A small per-nation-pair scalar (-1..1) seeded at generation from shared borders/resource competition, drifting slowly from corp activity (heavy extraction in a nation nudges its sentiment toward the extracting corp's home nation). Read-only input to licence cost/availability; no diplomacy UI for the prototype's follow-on scope.
3. **Historical fragmentation.** Exclaves and disputed zones are a **generation-time** decoration on top of BL-053's Voronoi/merge output — after merge, some tiles are deliberately left owned by a non-contiguous or disputed neighbour rather than reassigned, for flavour and to justify uneven licence friction. Not a simulated historical event log.
4. **Non-Kepler jurisdiction.** Off-Earth bodies (once Era 1 opens them) start with no nation ownership — jurisdiction there is corp-claim-based, not nation-based; this item only needs to state that boundary, not design the space-claim system (that's Era 1 scope, BL-087-adjacent).

items.title: Economy bankruptcy test — calibrate costs to a 10–20 year runway
items.summary: Headless harness that runs economy ticks from world-gen to bankruptcy (cash <= 0), records tick count per run, and outputs a per-building / per-resource data table. Goal: tune costs so the average player goes bankrupt in 10–20 in-game years without intervention — use the data to derive sensible build costs and running expenses.
items.design:
A `tools/verify/econ_bankruptcy.cpp` harness (same pattern as existing headless checks) that:

1. Calls `make_hard_coded_world()` to get a reproducible starting state.
2. Ticks `economy_system` until the player corporation cash <= 0 (or a ceiling tick, e.g. 500 years, to catch non-bankrupt runs).
3. Records: total ticks to bankruptcy, in-game years elapsed, and for each building: cash burn per tick attributed to that building type, and for each resource: net flow (production minus consumption) per tick.
4. Prints a structured report: summary row (years to bankruptcy), then per-building and per-resource rows.

Design owed: define bankruptcy precisely (cash <= 0? unable to pay maintenance for N consecutive ticks?); agree on the ceiling; decide whether to vary starting conditions (different body selections, building counts) or fix them. Once the harness runs, use the output table to set build costs and maintenance values such that an unmanaged player reaches bankruptcy in 10–20 years on average.

**Design settled (2026-06-16):** Bankruptcy trigger: the corporation cannot cover its maintenance / running costs (interest) for a tick, AND balance is at or below **-5 × start_money** (deep-red threshold, not just any negative balance). Open design note: add a **debt-interest system** — when balance goes negative, charge interest each tick, making deep-red increasingly punishing; record as a follow-on item. Starting conditions: **fixed** (hard-coded world, same building set every run) for test reproducibility. Seeded variation (different building counts or random seeds) is recorded as a future extension but not part of the initial harness. Ceiling: a configurable tick ceiling (e.g. 500 in-game years) for non-bankrupt runs.

items.title: Cross-platform build (Linux + Windows)
items.summary: Linux+Windows build. Source already Linux-clean (FetchContent deps, LUA_USE_POSIX guarded) except src/ui/fonts.cpp's hardcoded Windows font paths; fix = bundle assets/fonts + SDL_GetBasePath prepend, Windows paths as fallback. Headless tier builds anywhere; GitHub Actions both-OS headless CI as the guard. Dev moves to Linux (dual-boot); visual-verify offscreen (dummy+software renderer / Xvfb) is a deferred spike. [COMPLETE 2026-06-30: native Linux GCC-14 build confirmed (C language enabled, sol2 v3.5.0); Windows + dual-GCC CI green; advisory Xvfb visual-verify job added.]
items.design:
**Origin.** Linux + Windows cross-platform was original CONCEPT scope. Surfaced 2026-06-17 while wanting to run the build/verify loop from the Cowork Linux sandbox; Ben will move primary development to Linux (machine is dual-boot).

**Finding — the source is already Linux-clean.** Audited all 93 `src/*` files: no `windows.h`, `WinMain`, `__declspec`, `_WIN32`/`_MSC_VER` guards, or `MAX_PATH`. Every dependency is cross-platform and acquired via CMake `FetchContent` (SDL3 release-3.2.0, Lua 5.4.7, sol2 v3.3.0, ImGui v1.91.6) — no vcpkg / system-package assumptions. `CMakeLists.txt` already guards Lua's `LUA_USE_POSIX` under `if(UNIX)`. So this is a build-environment job, not a source port — with one exception.

**The one source gap — font loading.** `src/ui/fonts.cpp` hardcodes Windows system fonts (`C:/Windows/Fonts/segoeui.ttf`, tahoma, arial, verdana); `fonts.hpp` already flags this as Windows-only per TECH_FOUNDATIONS and names the intended fix. Fix: bundle a redistributable TTF under `assets/fonts/`, resolve it relative to the executable (`SDL_GetBasePath`) and prepend it to the candidate list; keep the Windows paths as a trailing fallback so Windows builds are unchanged. Built-in ProggyClean stays the final fallback. Small and self-contained — but it changes `src/` and renders in the GUI, so it must be visually verified on a real build (i.e. on Ben's Linux box), not blind-shipped from the sandbox.

**Tiers — what runs where.**
- *Headless tier* (`tools/verify/*.cpp` over `world/*`, deliberately SDL/Lua/ImGui-free): builds anywhere with g++/cmake. Already portable; nothing owed. The Cowork/CI-friendly target.
- *Windowed app on Linux*: needs cmake + SDL3 build deps (X11/Wayland + GL dev headers) + the font fix. No code changes beyond fonts. Runnable natively once Ben is on Linux.
- *Visual-verify tier* (`ProjectIo --verify` → PNG golden diff): `app.cpp` creates a real `SDL_Window` + `SDL_CreateRenderer`, so it runs natively on a Linux desktop. For *headless CI* it needs offscreen rendering (`SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy` + the SDL software renderer feeding `SDL_RenderReadPixels` → `png_writer`), else an Xvfb virtual display. **Open spike:** confirm dummy + software-renderer pixel readback under SDL3 3.2.0; fall back to Xvfb in CI if it won't read back. Contained — blocks neither the headless tier nor native Linux runs.

**Settled decisions (2026-06-17).**
- *Primary dev OS → Linux* (Ben's dual-boot machine). Makes native GUI + visual-verify available locally and flips Windows to the at-risk platform.
- *CI → GitHub Actions, both OS, headless tier now.* Build `ubuntu-latest` + `windows-latest` and run the headless harnesses on push — the standing guard against Windows drift now that dev is Linux-side. Cache `FetchContent` deps to keep runs cheap. Visual-verify is added to CI **after** the offscreen spike, not on day one.

**Recommended sequence.**
1. Font portability fix (`assets/fonts/*.ttf` + candidate-list change) — unblocks any Linux GUI/visual build. *(touches src — verify the render on Linux.)*
2. Confirm a native Linux configure+build of the full app; document the recipe (cmake + SDL3 deps) in TECH_FOUNDATIONS.
3. CI workflow: ubuntu + windows build + headless harnesses, with dep caching.
4. Offscreen-render spike; if green, add the visual-verify tier to CI.

**Out of scope:** packaging/installers, macOS, broader runtime asset-path overhaul beyond fonts.

**Cowork-session note (2026-06-17):** the design above is settled here, but the build/verify steps cannot be exercised in the Cowork sandbox (no cmake, no SDL3 deps, ephemeral dep re-pull). Execution — font edit, native build, CI YAML — lands on Ben's Linux box or in CI itself.

items.title: Git hygiene for the Cowork-shell bridge (line endings + native-commit rule)
items.summary: Two git footguns when running git inside the Cowork shell (VM bridge): CRLF blobs vs LF mount -> whole-file diff churn; .git blocks unlink/rename -> stale lock files + unsafe ref writes. Fix: add .gitattributes (* text=auto) + one-time renormalize for the CRLF half; standing rule that git WRITES run from native Claude Code / terminal, never the Cowork shell. Part 2 dissolves under native Linux dev (BL-057).
items.design:
**Origin.** Surfaced 2026-06-17 trying to commit BL-057 from the Cowork shell; previously hit on Project-Fulcrum and wrongly assumed resolved. The cause is structural (the Cowork file bridge), not per-repo, so it recurs across projects.

**Problem — two independent failure modes when git *writes* run inside the Cowork shell.** The shell is a sandboxed Linux VM with the Windows repo bridged in via a sync/mount layer; the file tools (Read/Write/Edit) hit the real folder, the shell sees a mirror.
1. *Line endings.* Repo blobs are CRLF (native Windows checkout) but files surface in the mount as LF/mixed, so every `git add` becomes a whole-file line-ending diff — e.g. CMakeLists showed 289 changed lines for a ~9-line edit; REFINED 1161; requirements 2678. The real change is buried and the commit is junk.
2. *`.git` permissions.* The mount blocks unlink/rename inside `.git`: git can write loose objects but cannot remove temp files or `*.lock` refs, so it leaves stale `HEAD.lock` / `refs/heads/main.lock` and cannot safely update a ref (`Operation not permitted`).

Net: git writes (add/commit/merge/push) from the shell corrupt diffs and/or wedge the repo. Content edits via the file tools are safe; git is not.

**Fix — two parts.**
1. *Line-ending hardening (repo).* Add a `.gitattributes` — `* text=auto`, plus explicit binary rules (`*.ttf binary`, and any other binaries) — then run a one-time `git add --renormalize .` so blobs become canonical LF while Windows working trees stay CRLF via autocrlf. Removes the diff-churn half. The renormalize is a single deliberate repo-wide commit; do it on its own, native, not bundled with feature work.
2. *Standing rule (process).* Record that **git writes must run from native Claude Code or a native terminal, never the Cowork shell** — the shell is for content edits (file tools) and read-only inspection only. Lands in `.claude/rules/io-standing-rules.md` § Working method when actioned; cross-ref from CLAUDE.md.

**Note.** Part 2 is fully dissolved once development moves to native Linux Claude Code (no VM, no bridge) — see BL-057 — but the rule still matters for any Cowork-shell session. Part 1 (`.gitattributes`) is worth doing regardless as CRLF hygiene for the Linux/Windows split.

**Out of scope.** The `.git` unlink/permission limitation is a property of the Cowork bridge, not fixable in-repo; the standing rule is the mitigation.

items.title: Application-driven mouse — scriptable cursor override for deterministic capture
items.summary: A verify/app-controlled synthetic cursor so the real OS mouse position cannot leak into --verify captures (hover highlight + hover-card perturb the frame -> flaky goldens). Also the foundation for scripted pointer input (move/click/drag) in the verify harness. Design owed: synthetic-vs-real source switch, global hover-suppress vs explicit positioning, click/drag API surface. [COMPLETE 2026-06-30: application-driven mouse (ui_state::mouse + verify Lua mouse()/hover_tile()) shipped; OS cursor suppressed in --verify captures.]
items.design:
**Problem.** Headless `--verify` captures read the live `ImGui::GetIO().MousePos`, so wherever the real OS cursor happens to sit leaks into the frame as a hovered-tile highlight (and the hover-card). A cursor that moves between or during captures changes the rendered frame -> golden flake. Observed in the Lens & Legibility batch (2026-06-17): the draw-order sort fixed the `unordered_map` half of the nondeterminism, but a moving mouse is the other half. See [[reference_worktree_gui_build]].

**Proposal.** An **application-driven mouse**: a single source-of-truth cursor position the canvases consume instead of the raw IO mouse, with an override the verify harness (and later scripted input) sets. In `--verify`, hover is **off by default** (no synthetic position) and a script opts in with an explicit `verify.mouse(x,y)` / `verify.hover_tile(col,row)`; in the live app the source is the real mouse. This makes captures deterministic regardless of the OS cursor and is the groundwork for **scripted pointer input** (move/click/drag) the verify harness currently lacks.

**Open questions (design owed):** where the synthetic-vs-real switch lives (ui_state flag? a thin input source abstraction?); whether to suppress hover globally in verify or require explicit positioning; whether to generalise to full scripted click/drag now or stub the API; interaction with the existing `verify.center_tile`/`canvas_command` vocabulary. Pairs with [[the hotkey/input system]] (BL: HOTKEY_SYSTEM) — both want a small input-dispatch layer. Relates to the determinism work landed in the lens batch.

items.design:
**Problem.** Input bindings are scattered and partly hardcoded: the `canvas_command` vocabulary (pan/zoom/ascend/descend/body+lens cycle) plus hardcoded keys (Space = pause, 1-5 = speed, lens cycle), with no single place a player or developer can see or change them. There is no discoverability and no rebinding.

**Proposal (to design).** A **unified hotkey system**: one central **action -> binding** keymap that every input flows through, covering canvas navigation, lens selection (the curated strip + cycle), time control, ledger/panel toggles, and build/placement. Rebindable, with a **discoverable cheat-sheet / help overlay**. The existing `canvas_command` enum is a natural action vocabulary to build on / subsume.

**Open questions (design owed):** binding storage (a keymap file vs settings.json vs in-engine config); conflict detection and resolution; chord / modifier support; the help-overlay surface and how it lists bindings; **context scoping** (do bindings differ by canvas rung / modal state / placement mode?); whether `canvas_command` becomes the action layer or is replaced; player-facing rebinding UI vs developer-only config for the prototype. Bundled with [[the application-driven mouse]] (BL: APP_DRIVEN_MOUSE) as the project's input strand — both could share a small input-dispatch layer; sequence the keymap on top of, or alongside, that. Consider whether a dedicated `docs/ui/HOTKEYS.md` authority doc is warranted over MENU.md.

**Accessibility (2026-06-24 review).** This item is the **motor-accessibility** half of the prototype's accessibility strand: keyboard-complete operation is the single biggest win for players who cannot use a mouse precisely (the UI is otherwise mouse-only, with small targets — the icon nav rail, the tight time-control buttons, individual hexes), and **rebindable** bindings matter for switch-access and one-handed users. items.title: Selection info element — full-width bottom bar layout
items.summary: Redesign the Selection info element from a narrow bottom-left pinned panel to a full-width bar spanning the bottom of the screen, tall enough to show an entity portrait alongside multiple content sections simultaneously in one view. [COMPLETE 2026-06-30: full-width bottom selection bar with portrait column + summary/lens-supplement sections shipped (src/ui/selection_panel.cpp).]
items.design:
**Motivation.** The current spec pins the Selection element to the bottom-left, above the overlay strip, at the same compact height as the overlay controls. That height is insufficient to show an entity portrait (photo/emblem) alongside multiple stat sections at once — the user has to scroll or the content is hidden. A full-width bottom bar solves this: it keeps every section visible simultaneously and reserves a portrait column on the left.

**Layout proposal.**
```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ [Portrait] │ Header (name + type + icon) [Go To] [✕] │              │
│            ├──────────────────────────────────────────┤  Section C   │
│  (image /  │  Section A           │  Section B        │              │
│   emblem)  │  (primary stat block)│  (secondary info) │              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
- **Span**: full canvas width (nav rail to right edge), pinned to the bottom of the screen, above nothing (the overlay control strip is folded in or repositioned).
- **Height**: fixed at a value that accommodates a portrait plus 2–3 rows of text content simultaneously — approximately the height of 4–5 standard ImGui rows (tentative; tune during implementation).
- **Portrait column** (leftmost, fixed width ~80–100 px): entity image or emblem drawn via ImGui image or a placeholder glyph from `ui::icons` while real portraits are absent.
- **Content area** (remainder): split horizontally into two or three sections depending on selection kind. Each section is a vertical stack of labelled rows (using the shared content builders from `entity_summary`). The header row (name + type + icon + 'Go to' + close) spans the full content area at the top.
- **Overlay control strip**: currently bottom-left; with the bar taking the full bottom edge, the overlay strip either (a) moves to a floating position over the canvas (near the lens-icon cluster), or (b) is inlined into the bar when a selection is active and shown at its original position when nothing is selected. This is the main layout conflict to resolve at implementation time.

items.title: Survey system — bodies start unsurveyed; survey action reveals tile map + deposit bands
items.summary: v0.0.8 discovery strand. Bodies start unsurveyed: only type, orbital position and grid size are known. The player dispatches a survey (credits upfront) that plays out over sim ticks, revealing the body REGION-BY-REGION until surface + deposit bands are known; exact deposit amounts still wait for first extraction-site placement. Cost and duration scale with body size AND distance from home. No concurrency cap — credit cost is the throttle. Earth/home start surveyed. DESIGN SETTLED 2026-06-30 (BL-067).
items.design:
**Status:** design settled 2026-06-30. The four load-bearing calls (Ben): progressive
region-by-region reveal; pre-survey shows type+position+size only; cost AND duration scale with
size AND distance; no concurrency cap (credit cost is the throttle).

### The loop
A body starts `hidden` — the player sees only its **type**, **orbital position** (already on the
Solar canvas) and **grid size**, never its tiles or deposits. Selecting it shows a **cost + ETA
preview**; dispatching debits credits from the player corp **upfront** and the survey then plays out
over sim ticks, **revealing the body one region at a time** until the whole surface and its deposit
**richness bands** (rich / moderate / sparse, per ROADMAP) are known. Exact deposit *amounts* still
wait for first extraction-site placement (roadmap-settled — unchanged here).

### Reveal model (progressive by region)
- The tile grid is partitioned into **regions** by a fixed **super-cell size** `S` (≈ 8×8 tiles):
  `regions = ceil(grid_width/S) × ceil(grid_height/S)`. Region count therefore **scales with body
  size** — a big planet has many regions, a small asteroid only a few — each region a roughly
  uniform chunk of tiles.
- Regions are revealed **one at a time in a deterministic raster order** (row-major over region
  cells). **No RNG** anywhere in the reveal — the order is a pure function of grid dimensions, so it
  satisfies the determinism rule. `regions_done` alone determines exactly which tiles are visible
  (tile is visible iff its region's reveal-index < `regions_done`).
- On the Planetary canvas, **unrevealed regions are masked** (dark/locked overlay); revealed regions
  render normally. A region's deposit bands become known when that region completes.

### Cost & duration (size × distance)
- **Distance** `D` = `|r_body − r_home|` where `r` is **heliocentric orbital radius** (`orbital_radius_au`;
  a moon uses its **parent's** radius). Static and legible — chosen over live Euclidean distance,
  which would drift as bodies orbit and make the preview non-reproducible.
- **Size** `T` = tile count (`grid_width × grid_height`).
- **Cost (credits, debited upfront at dispatch):**
  `cost = base_dispatch + dist_cost_per_au·D + scan_cost_per_tile·T`
- **Duration** splits into two phases so distance reads as *lead time* and size as *scan time*:
  - `transit_ticks = base_transit + transit_per_au·D` — probe en route; **nothing revealed yet**.
  - `scan_ticks    = base_scan + scan_per_tile·T` — regions reveal **evenly** across this phase;
    region *k* completes at `transit_ticks + round(k/regions_total · scan_ticks)`.
  - `total = transit_ticks + scan_ticks`.
- Starting constants are placeholders to **calibrate in a headless harness** (target feel: a near
  small asteroid is cheap/fast; a far large planet is very expensive and slow). One sim tick = one day.

### Data model
```cpp
enum class survey_phase : uint8_t { hidden, in_transit, scanning, surveyed };
struct survey_state {
    survey_phase phase           = survey_phase::hidden;
    int          regions_total   = 0;  // computed at dispatch from grid + super-cell S
    int          regions_done    = 0;  // revealed so far (reveal order deterministic)
    int          ticks_remaining = 0;  // until the next phase / region boundary
};
```
- Carried **inline on `body_component`** (bodies are few — ~a dozen — so no separate map needed).
- `world.home_body` starts `surveyed` (`regions_done = regions_total`); if Earth is a distinct named
  body it starts surveyed too. All others `hidden`.
- **No concurrency cap:** many bodies may be `in_transit`/`scanning` at once — each carries its own
  `survey_state`, so unlimited concurrency falls out for free; the credit cost is the only limiter.

### Survey system (deterministic tick)
- New `src/world/survey_system.{hpp,cpp}`: `advance_surveys(world&, int days)` called each sim tick.
  For every body not `hidden`/`surveyed`, decrement `ticks_remaining`, cross phase boundaries
  (`in_transit → scanning → surveyed`) and bump `regions_done` as scan-phase region boundaries pass.
  Pure, deterministic, **no RNG, no Lua, no per-tile data exposed to Lua**.
- **Dispatch** `dispatch_survey(world&, entity_id body) -> survey_dispatch_result` (success /
  insufficient_funds / already_surveyed / in_progress): checks player balance, debits upfront,
  computes `regions_total` + schedule, sets `phase = in_transit`. The debit is a one-off balance
  decrement now; it becomes a labelled expenditure line when the v0.0.9 budget breakdown lands.
- Mutation is **centralised in app** (the UI surfaces hold `const world&`), mirroring the construction
  request seam: the Selection-panel button sets a pending request that `app::render` executes.

### UI surfaces
- **Solar canvas** (`solar_system_canvas.cpp`): per-body **survey badge** — `hidden`: dimmed + `?`
  glyph; `in_transit`/`scanning`: small progress arc or `k∕N` region count; `surveyed`: normal.
  New glyph(s) in `ui::icons` (badge + `?`), per ICONS.md recipe.
- **Planetary canvas** (`body_surface_canvas.cpp`): **mask unrevealed regions** (locked overlay);
  revealed regions render normally; a small header progress read while scanning.
- **Selection panel** (`selection_panel.cpp`): a **Survey section** keyed on body state —
  `hidden`: `Dispatch Survey — <cost> cr · ETA <days> d` button (preview from size+distance);
  `in_transit`: `En route — ETA <days> d`; `scanning`: `Surveying <k>/<N> · ETA <days> d`;
  `surveyed`: `Surveyed.` Disabled with reason when the player can't afford it.

### Determinism & serialisation seams
- Region partition and reveal order are **pure functions of grid dimensions** + fixed `S` — no RNG,
  reproducible across runs.
- The four `survey_state` fields **join the flat-binary serialisation** read+write paths symmetrically
  when that path exists (no save/load wired in `world/*` yet — flag at integration so survey state is
  not silently dropped from a future snapshot).

### Scope / requirements (Full mode)
Item-spanning requirement group authored before decomposition:
- **`visual`** — a `scripts/verify/survey.lua` capture sequence: unsurveyed body masked on the
  Planetary canvas → partial reveal after N ticks (some regions visible, some masked) → full reveal;
  plus the Solar-canvas badge in each state.
- **`headless`** — a `tools/verify/survey_*.cpp` harness asserting: cost/duration formulas vs size+distance,
  deterministic region partition + raster reveal order (same grid → same order), `home_body` starts
  surveyed, and unlimited concurrent surveys advance independently.

### Deferred extensions (out of scope here)
Abortable per-region payment / refund; landing-point-seeded reveal order (instead of raster);
rival/AI surveying (standing rule keeps AI a data-model stub); survey as a budget line (v0.0.9).

Verified: survey_harness R2-R6 (41 asserts PASS); survey.lua 4 goldens PASS 0.0000%. Design propagated to systems.md/SOLAR/PLANETARY/SELECTION/ICONS/GLOSSARY. items.title: Visibility model — competitor info asymmetry (markers public, production/stockpile private, markets public)
items.summary: v0.0.8 discovery strand. Competitor information asymmetry as a READ-TIME access policy over existing data (no new stored state). Rival building markers visible only where the body's survey has revealed their region; rival hover cards show type + owner only; selecting a rival building opens a dedicated competitor panel with explicit 'private' placeholders for production/stockpile; market aggregates + prices stay public (the intelligence channel). Uniform rule: anything not player-owned is opaque. Requires BL-067. DESIGN SETTLED 2026-06-30 (BL-068).
items.design:
**Status:** design settled 2026-06-30. `requires` BL-067 (survey). Calls (Ben): rival markers
visible **only on surveyed bodies**; hover card **type + owner only**; selecting a rival opens a
**dedicated competitor panel** (public facts + explicit 'private' placeholders); **uniform** branch —
not player-owned ⇒ opaque.

### The core idea
The economy is interactive but trivially legible; this makes the player **not omniscient**. They
spend to survey (BL-067), then read **public market signals** to infer private competitor state. The
rule is a **read-time access policy** — it changes what the UI is *allowed to render*, not what the
simulation stores. **No new stored fields, no tick logic, no determinism or serialisation impact.**

### Ownership is already tracked — only an accessor is new
Ownership lives in `corporation_component::assets` (a `vector<entity_id>` of owned buildings),
maintained at runtime: `construction.cpp` appends player-built buildings to the player corp's
`assets` (line ~71), exactly as generation seeds rival assets. There is **no reverse index**, so add
two world helpers (siblings of `pool_for` / `workforce_supply`):
```cpp
entity_id owner_corp_of (const world&, entity_id building);   // scans corps' assets (~dozen corps); null_entity if unowned
bool      is_player_owned(const world&, entity_id building);   // owner_corp_of(...) -> corporations.at(corp).is_player
```
`is_player_owned` is the single branch point for the whole feature (answer 4: **uniform** — everyone
not the player is treated identically). A reverse `building_to_corp` map (mirroring `tile_to_nation`)
is an optional O(1) backing if profiling ever warrants; the accessor is the stable seam either way.

### The visibility rule (canonical table)
| Channel | Visibility for a RIVAL entity |
|---|---|
| Building marker / presence | **Public**, but only once survey has revealed its tile's region (see below) |
| Building **type** + **owner** corp name | **Public** |
| Production rate / recipe throughput | **Private** |
| Stockpile quantities | **Private** |
| Per-body market supply/demand aggregates + prices | **Public** — the sanctioned intelligence channel |

Player-owned entities are fully visible (unchanged: management detail, output, workforce, stockpile).

### 1. Marker visibility — composed with survey region-reveal (answer 1: surveyed only)
A marker is visible **iff its tile sits in a survey-revealed region** of its body. This piggybacks on
BL-067's region mask — no separate rival gate: on an unsurveyed body nothing shows; during partial
survey a rival marker appears only when its region is revealed; on a fully-surveyed body all markers
(yours and rivals') show. `body_surface_canvas` already iterates buildings to place markers and
register hit-zones — add the `region-revealed?` predicate to that pass so masked-region buildings
are neither drawn nor hit-testable.

### 2. Hover card — type + owner only (answer 2)
BL-020 shipped `hover_content.cpp` with (kind × lens) exemplars. The building hover branches on
`is_player_owned`:
- **player-owned** → existing full detail (type, target/recipe, output, workforce).
- **rival** → `"<Building type> · <owner corp name>"` and nothing else. No production, no stockpile.

`corporation_component::name` supplies the owner string; the rival's identity colour (already used by
the Corporation lens / marker tint) carries through unchanged.

### 3. Selection panel — dedicated competitor layout (answer 3)
`selection_panel.cpp` branches on `is_player_owned` for a selected building:
- **player-owned** → existing management layout (workforce target, recipe, decommission).
- **rival** → a **competitor layout**: public facts (building type, owner corp, body/tile location,
  and the body's **public** market context) **plus explicit teaching rows** —
  `Production: ▁ private` and `Stockpile: ▁ private` — that render the *withheld* channels as
  visible placeholders rather than silently omitting them. The panel never leaks more than the hover
  card's facts; the 'private' rows make the asymmetry legible and teach the rule.

### 4. Markets stay public — no market-ledger change
Per-body market aggregates and prices remain fully public; the Market/Balance ledgers are unchanged.
This item only *names* the market as the intended inference channel — the player reasons "a rising
price in a good Kepler is known to extract means their output is down" from public data, never from a
private panel. Keeping markets untouched holds the scope tight.

### Files & scope (Full mode, but light — read-side only)
`world.{hpp,cpp}` (the two accessors), `hover_content.{hpp,cpp}` (rival branch),
`selection_panel.cpp` (competitor layout), `body_surface_canvas.cpp` (marker region-reveal predicate).
No data-model, tick, determinism, or serialisation changes. Item-spanning requirement: a **`visual`**
check (`scripts/verify/visibility.lua`) — on a surveyed body, a rival building shows a type+owner
hover and a competitor selection panel with `private` placeholders, and **never** renders
production/stockpile; a player building still shows full management detail; a rival building in an
unrevealed region is absent. A small **`headless`** check may assert `owner_corp_of` /
`is_player_owned` resolve generated and player-built buildings correctly.

### Deferred extensions (out of scope)
Relationship tiers (allied / neutral / rival visibility) — the uniform `is_player` branch is the
prototype rule, with the accessor as the natural later extension point; market-signal *inference
tooling* (highlighting which rival a price move implicates); rivals actually *reacting* to the player
(standing rule keeps AI a data-model stub); unit/convoy visibility (folds in when units exist).

items.title: Population legibility — surface habitability→workforce reasoning in lens / hover / selection
items.summary: v0.0.8 discovery strand — surfacing only, no new mechanics. Makes the existing habitability→workforce feedback legible so the player can reason about siting. Surfaced in the Selection panel, hover cards, AND the Population lens. Workforce cap shown as an absolute number. The Population lens is RE-KEYED from raw habitability to workforce efficiency via a shared workforce_efficiency(habitability) helper that the economy system also uses (so the lens shows exactly the consequence the sim applies). DESIGN SETTLED 2026-06-30 (BL-069).
items.design:
**Status:** design settled 2026-06-30. **Surfacing only — no new simulation.** Calls (Ben):
surface in Selection panel + hover + lens (all three); express the workforce cap as an **absolute
number**; **re-key the Population lens to workforce-cap** (not raw habitability).

### What already simulates (the chain we're making legible)
- `population_centre_component`: `scale` (1–5), `population` (thousands), `habitability` (0–1 from tile).
- `economy_system.cpp` computes a **scale-weighted mean habitability per body** (`report.body_habitability`)
  and applies a **habitability-efficiency curve** to effective workforce (`workforce_contention`):
  `hab_scalar = (hab >= 0.6) ? 1.0 : (0.5 + (hab/0.6)*0.5)` — full labour at/above 0.6, ramping to
  0.5× at habitability 0. This **curve is the "workforce cap"** the player reasons about for siting.
- Effective workforce a corp's buildings contend for = `workforce_supply(corp, body) × hab_scalar(body)`.

Nothing here changes — this item only *shows* it.

### The one structural change — a shared efficiency helper (correctness, not mechanics)
Extract the curve into **`src/world/workforce.hpp`**:
```cpp
/// Habitability → workforce-efficiency multiplier. Single source of truth shared by
/// the economy system and the Population lens so the lens shows exactly what the sim applies.
inline float workforce_efficiency(float habitability) {
    return habitability >= 0.6f ? 1.0f : 0.5f + (habitability / 0.6f) * 0.5f;
}
```
`economy_system.cpp` refactors its inline expression to call this (behaviour-identical — guarded by a
headless regression check). The re-keyed lens calls the **same** helper, so it cannot drift from the
simulation by a duplicated constant. This is the load-bearing decision that makes "re-key to
workforce-cap" *correct* rather than a lookalike.

### 1. Population lens — re-keyed to workforce efficiency (answer 3)
`overlay_mode::population` in `body_surface_canvas.cpp` currently tints each tile by **raw
habitability** (`0.15 + 0.7·h` green ramp). Re-key it to tint by **`workforce_efficiency(tile.habitability)`**:
tiles at/above 0.6 read at full labour (flat green); below 0.6 grade down sharply — so the lens shows
the **efficiency cliff at 0.6**, exactly the siting signal ("build where habitability ≥ 0.6 for full
workforce"). The tint stays per-tile (faithful to the lens model) but now communicates the
*consequence*, not the input. Update `draw_population_key` and the lens tooltip
(`overlay.cpp`) from "habitability" to **"workforce efficiency"**.

### 2. Selection panel — population-centre / tile workforce read (answers 1, 2)
`selection_panel.cpp`: when a population centre (or a tile carrying one) is selected, show:
- **Scale** with its label (village → town → city → conurbation → metropolis),
- **Population** (headcount, thousands),
- **Local habitability** (0–1, its own row),
- **Workforce cap** as an **absolute number** (answer 2 — value only, *no* "— low habitability"
  annotation): the body's effective workforce for the player corp =
  `workforce_supply(player_corp, body) × workforce_efficiency(body_habitability)`, read from the
  economy report the panel already consumes. Habitability is a separate row, so the causal datum is
  present without annotating the cap field itself.

### 3. Hover cards — quick workforce tell (answer 1)
`hover_content.cpp` (BL-020 vocabulary): add a **Tile × Population** exemplar — hovering a tile under
the Population lens gives a glance read: habitability + the workforce-cap number. Consistent with the
existing (kind × lens) hover pattern; graceful fallback elsewhere unchanged.

### Files & scope (Full mode, light — surfacing + one shared-helper refactor)
`workforce.hpp` (new helper), `economy_system.cpp` (refactor to the helper),
`body_surface_canvas.cpp` (lens re-key + key), `selection_panel.cpp` (workforce read),
`hover_content.{hpp,cpp}` (Tile×Population exemplar), `overlay.cpp` (lens tooltip text). No new stored
state; **no determinism or serialisation impact** (the helper refactor is behaviour-preserving).
Item-spanning requirements:
- **`headless`** — assert `workforce_efficiency` reproduces the prior inline curve **exactly** across
  the habitability range (regression guard on the economy-system refactor — this is the only place we
  touch shipped simulation code).
- **`visual`** — `scripts/verify/population_legibility.lua`: the Population lens shows the 0.6
  efficiency cliff; the Selection panel on a centre shows scale / population / habitability / workforce-cap
  number; the hover shows the quick read.

### Deferred extensions (out of scope)
Constraint-reason annotation on the cap (we chose absolute-only); per-corp workforce breakdown beyond
the player corp; population-growth projection legibility; surfacing the food-demand gate that also
throttles growth.
items.resolution: Delivered (v0.0.8). Surfacing + one behaviour-preserving refactor: extracted the habitability→workforce curve into src/world/workforce.hpp (single source of truth); economy_system.cpp calls it (bit-identical, determinism preserved); Population lens + draw_population_key re-keyed to workforce efficiency and overlay.cpp tooltip relabelled (shows the 0.6 cliff); Selection panel population-centre read (scale/population/local habitability + absolute workforce cap) in selection_panel.cpp; Tile×Population hover exemplar in hover_content.{hpp,cpp}. Verified: workforce_harness (1001-sample exact-curve regression PASS); population_legibility.lua 3 goldens PASS 0.0000%; population_lens.lua re-blessed to the efficiency tint.

items.summary: There is no in-app menu for application-level control: today the only way to leave the game is the OS window close button (Windows-only chrome; the window is a plain SDL_WINDOW_RESIZABLE in app.cpp) or a keyboard shortcut. The player wants a minimal, clickable system container — at minimum an Exit Game affordance, reachable without memorising hotkeys and consistent across platforms. Distinct from BL-062 (the keyboard hotkey system) and from the nav-rail ledger menus (MENU.md): those are the keyboard layer and the per-system ledgers; this is the application/session shell (start, pause, exit). Design owed: the surface (top menu bar vs. corner gear button vs. centred pause/system modal), what it contains in the prototype (Exit Game at minimum; likely Resume/Pause; possibly New/Restart), whether a confirm-on-exit is wanted, and how it relates to a future title/main screen.
items.design:
**Problem.** The app has no application-level menu. Exit is only via the OS title-bar close button — which is Windows-only chrome and absent on a borderless/other-platform build — or a keyboard shortcut. A player should be able to leave (and later start/restart) the game by clicking, without knowing any hotkey. This is the session shell, deliberately separate from the nav-rail ledgers (broad per-system overviews, MENU.md) and from BL-062's rebindable keymap (the keyboard layer over the same actions).

**Scope for the prototype (minimum).** A clickable **Exit Game** that cleanly tears down (the same path as the window-close / quit event). Pair it with **Pause/Resume** so the session-control verbs sit together. New/Restart and a full title screen are out of scope here — name them as the natural follow-on once a title/main screen lands.

**Options for the surface (advisor call — pick at promotion):**

A) **ImGui main menu bar** (BeginMainMenuBar) across the top with a Game menu (Exit, Pause). Cheapest; conventional; but it eats a strip of vertical space above the header panel and must be reconciled with the existing top-row layout (profile + header + time column).

B) **Corner gear/hamburger button** that opens a small popup with the same items. Minimal footprint, no permanent chrome; fits the icon-rail visual language already used by the nav pane. **Recommended starting point** — lowest layout disruption.

C) **Centred pause/system modal** toggled by Esc and by a button: dims the canvas and lists Resume / Exit (the classic pause menu). Best long-term home for session control and where a title screen would converge, but more than the minimum asks.

**Open questions.** Confirm-on-exit (a 'really quit?' guard) yes/no; whether Esc should open option C even in the minimum build; whether this slot should also surface Save/Load once serialisation has a UI (currently save is not player-exposed). Authority: extend docs/ui/MENU.md with an 'Application / system menu' section when this lands (it currently documents only the nav-rail ledgers).

**Note.** A standing development practice is the per-milestone ImGui panel rule (DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES.md) — this surface is a candidate panel for the milestone it lands in. The OS window is created plain-resizable in app.cpp (SDL_CreateWindow(..., SDL_WINDOW_RESIZABLE)); this item does not change the OS window, it adds an in-app affordance over it.

### Resolved (2026-07-04, Ben — v0.0.9 design session)
- **Surface = B (corner gear popup).** A gear/hamburger button in a screen corner opens a small popup; lowest layout disruption, reuses the nav-rail icon language, adds no permanent chrome. A (top menu bar) and C (centred pause modal) rejected for the prototype minimum — C is the right long-term home once a title screen lands; revisit it then.
- **Contents (prototype minimum):** Exit Game + Pause/Resume. Pause mirrors the existing Space-hotkey pause state, so popup and keyboard drive one shared session-control flag (not two). New/Restart and a title screen stay the named follow-on.
- **Esc = toggles the same popup** — cheap keyboard parity without building option C's dimmed modal. (If C is ever built, Esc migrates onto it.)
- **Confirm-on-exit = yes**, inline in the same popup (Exit → 'Really quit?'), not a separate modal — there is no save and exit is destructive.
- **Save/Load = out of scope** — save is not player-exposed yet; the popup is the reserved home for it once serialisation gets a UI.
- **Files:** `src/core/app.cpp` (draw the corner button + popup; wire Exit to the existing quit/window-close path, Pause to the sim-pause flag), `src/ui/ui_state.hpp` (popup-open + confirm-pending flags). Authority on landing: add an 'Application / system menu' section to `docs/ui/MENU.md`.
- Status → **designed** (promote-ready). Difficulty holds at 2.

items.title: Build legibility — selected-tile affordances + 'why not here' placement reasons
items.summary: Gameplay-clarity strand (filed 2026-06-30): 'it's not clear where buildings can be built'. BL-010's placement-suitability surface tints tiles only once a build is ARMED; the player still can't tell what a tile affords beforehand, nor WHY a tinted-invalid tile is rejected. Surfacing only, no new placement mechanics: (1) a selected-tile affordance readout (terrain, deposits subject to survey state, territory owner, and which building types thrive / are valid / are invalid here); (2) rejection reasons — placement_rules returns a REASON (wrong terrain / no deposit / occupied / outside territory / slot full) instead of a bare bool, surfaced when an armed build hovers an invalid tile.
items.design:
**Delivered 2026-07-01.** Placement reason codes (placement_result / placement_reason, implicit-bool so existing call sites are untouched); the always-on selected-tile affordance readout (Thrives/Valid/Invalid + territory owner); the reason-coded build front door; and the armed why-not-here canvas label -- all wired and visually verified via scripts/verify/build_legibility.lua (goldens blessed). Design propagated to docs/ui/SELECTION.md (+ docs/ui/LENSES.md cross-note).

**Status:** design-owed — filed from a gameplay-clarity review (Ben, 2026-06-30). Captures intent; load-bearing calls below are open.

### Problem
The placement-suitability surface (BL-010, complete) tints affinity tiles, but only **after** a building type is armed in the construction panel. Two legibility gaps remain:
1. **Before arming** the player has no read on what a given tile is good for — they must arm each building in turn and eyeball the tint.
2. **When a tile is invalid** the surface greys it but never says *why*, so the player can't tell a fixable problem (unsurveyed, occupied) from a fundamental one (wrong terrain).

### Proposed surfacing (no new mechanics)
- **Selected-tile affordance readout** (Selection panel / tile inspector): for the selected tile show terrain composition+landform, deposits (respecting survey state — bands not exact amounts pre-extraction), territory owner, and a short **"thrives / valid / invalid"** grouping of building types for that tile. This is the inverse of BL-010: BL-010 answers "given a building, which tiles?"; this answers "given a tile, which buildings?".
- **Rejection reasons**: refactor `placement_rules` to return a result carrying a **reason code** (enum + human string) rather than a bool — wrong terrain, no required deposit, tile occupied, outside player territory, building-slot full, unsurveyed. Surface the reason on the hover card (or Selection panel) when build mode is armed over an invalid tile.

### Open calls (Ben)
- Reasons shown on the **hover card** vs the **Selection panel** vs both.
- Whether to also add a **build-picker palette** that greys buildings unplaceable *anywhere* on the current body (bigger; could be a follow-on item).
- Whether the affordance readout is always-on for any selected tile, or only while build mode is armed.

### Authority
Lands into `docs/ui/SELECTION.md` (selected-tile content) with a cross-note in `docs/ui/LENSES.md` (the placement-suitability surface it complements). The reason-code refactor is a small change to the `placement_rules` seam (BL-043 authority).

### Resolved (2026-06-30, Ben)
- **Rejection reason surface = both.** The reason follows the cursor on the **hover card** while build mode is armed (where the eye is during placement), and also enriches the **Selection panel's** existing build-front-door line — which already prints a bare "Cannot build on water", so this swaps that string for reason-code text. No new state; both surfaces read the same `placement_result`.
- **Affordance readout = always-on** for any selected tile (not only while armed) — gap #1 is precisely that the player wants to read a tile *before* arming a building. Lives in the Selection panel: terrain composition + landform, deposits (survey-state-respecting bands, not exact amounts), territory owner, and a "thrives / valid / invalid" grouping of building types for that tile.
- **Reason-code refactor:** `can_place` / `can_place_in_world` return a `placement_result` — a reason enum (`ok`, `ocean`/`wrong_terrain`, `no_deposit`, `occupied`, `outside_territory`, `slot_full`, `unsurveyed`, `not_coastal`, `launchpad_exists`) plus a human string — with a `bool ok()` / implicit-bool conversion so the existing generation, construction and canvas-tint call sites compile unchanged. Reconcile with the overlapping result enum already in `construction.hpp` (`invalid_tile`): one vocabulary, not two.
- **Build-picker palette** (grey buildings unplaceable *anywhere* on the body) is **deferred to a follow-on** — bigger, and orthogonal to the per-tile read this item delivers.

items.title: Full budget breakdown — income vs expenditure itemised + projected runway
items.summary: v0.0.9 core strand (budget clarity) — directly answers 'how does the player make a profit'. The budget loop already computes balance += income − expenditure − maintenance − wages per corp (budget_system.hpp) but retains NO category split. Capture the four flows (and ideally by building type / resource / logistics) into the economy report, then surface an itemised income-vs-expenditure breakdown plus a running balance shown against a PROJECTED time-to-zero so the player feels the pressure and can act before bankruptcy.
items.design:
**Status:** design-owed — roadmap-named v0.0.9 strand, filed as a concrete item 2026-06-30.

### What exists
`apply_budget` (budget_system.hpp) already runs `balance += income − expenditure − maintenance − wages` per corp per tick, where income/expenditure are market cash flows at base_price, maintenance is flat per-building upkeep, and wages are `effective_workforce × base_wage`. The numbers are computed and discarded — only the net hits the balance.

### Proposed
1. **Capture** the four flows per corp into the economy report (retain at least the four-way split; ideally break income/expenditure **by building type and by resource**, and separate **logistics cost** once convoys charge it — BL-039/BL-045).
2. **Surface** an itemised breakdown in the Economy panel / Balance Ledger: income lines vs expenditure lines, netting to the per-tick delta the header already shows.
3. **Projected runway**: with the current per-tick delta and balance, show a **time-to-zero** (e.g. "runway: ~6 quarters at current burn") so negative deltas read as urgency, not just a falling number.

### Open calls (Ben)
- Granularity: four-way split (income/expenditure/maintenance/wages) as the MVP, or by-building/by-resource from the start.
- Runway basis: instantaneous last-tick delta (noisy) vs a smoothed trailing average (the trend plots from BL-066 suggest the smoothed form).
- Whether logistics cost is a distinct line now or deferred until convoy charging is itemised.

### Pairs with
[[BL-073]] debt interest (an expenditure line once balance is negative) and [[BL-074]] per-building profitability (the same captured flows, attributed to a single building). Settle the **flow-capture data shape once** for all three. Authority: `docs/development/ROADMAP.md` until v0.0.9 lands, then an economy/ledger doc.

### Resolved (2026-06-30, Ben)
- **Granularity:** four-way split per corp — income / expenditure / maintenance / wages (plus the [[BL-073]] interest line) — as the MVP. By-resource and by-building are deferred; by-building income is only ever an *estimate* against the pooled market (see [[BL-074]]), so it does not belong in the shared corp-level shape.
- **Data shape (settle-once for all three):** add a per-corp `corp_budget { income, expenditure, maintenance, wages, interest }` to the economy report, populated in `apply_budget` — which already computes maintenance and wages per building before collapsing them into the net `delta`. Income/expenditure come from the existing `corp_cash_flow`; the other flows are the budget step's own and just need retaining instead of discarding.
- **Runway basis:** smoothed trailing average of the net delta (pairs with the BL-066 trend store), not the noisy last-tick value. Surface as a `runway: ~N quarters` read beside the header NET, red when the trend is negative.
- **Logistics line:** deferred until convoys actually charge it (BL-039 / BL-045). Nothing to itemise today — reserve the line in the shape but do not populate it.

items.title: Debt-interest system — interest accrues on negative balance, visible as a budget line
items.summary: v0.0.9 strand. When a corp balance goes negative, interest accrues each tick — the econ_bankruptcy harness (BL-056) already models this for calibration, but no player-facing surface exists (grep for 'interest' in src/ returns nothing). Add the interest charge to apply_budget and surface it as a DISTINCT expenditure line in the budget breakdown so the player sees when they have entered a self-accelerating decline.
items.design:
**Status:** design-owed — roadmap-named v0.0.9 strand, filed 2026-06-30. Requires [[BL-072]] (it is a line in that breakdown).

### What exists
The `econ_bankruptcy` harness (BL-056) already models interest on a negative balance to calibrate a 10–20 year runway, but the live simulation does not charge it and nothing surfaces it. A grep for `interest`/`debt` across `src/` is empty — this is genuinely unbuilt in the running game.

### Proposed
- **Charge** interest in `apply_budget`: when `balance < 0`, `balance -= balance_owed × per_tick_rate`. Reuse the rate the bankruptcy harness calibrated so the harness and the live loop agree (single source of the constant).
- **Surface** it as its own expenditure line in the budget breakdown ([[BL-072]]) and, when active, a warning affordance in the header/balance area so the self-accelerating decline is unmistakable.

### Open calls (Ben)
- Rate source/value — confirm the bankruptcy-harness rate is the one to adopt, and where the constant lives (recipe_registry-style constants vs a budget constant).
- Whether interest compounds per tick or per quarter (determinism + legibility trade-off).
- Header treatment: a passive coloured balance vs an explicit "in debt — interest accruing" badge.

Determinism note: interest is a pure function of balance and a fixed rate — keep it in the deterministic `world/*` budget loop, no wall-clock.

### Resolved (2026-06-30, Ben)
- **Premise correction (important):** the filed text above is wrong that `econ_bankruptcy` "already models interest on a negative balance to calibrate a 10–20 year runway". It does **not** — the harness only measures time-to-zero from a fixed maintenance+wages burn; there is no interest charge or calibrated rate anywhere in `tools/verify/econ_bankruptcy.cpp`, and `grep interest src/` is empty. There was no rate to inherit, so we pick one.
- **Rate:** ~2 % per quarter (≈ 8 %/yr) on a negative balance — round, legible, corporate-distressed-debt feel. An underwater balance roughly doubles in ~9 years: real pressure without an unrecoverable death spiral.
- **Compounding:** charged once per economy tick on the current negative balance. A tick **is** a quarter (`k_ticks_per_year = 4`), so per-tick = per-quarter simple compounding. Pure function of balance × rate — stays in the deterministic `world/*` budget loop, no wall-clock.
- **Constant home:** one named constant (e.g. `k_debt_interest_per_quarter`) in a single header shared by the live budget loop **and** the bankruptcy harness, so the two never drift. Adopting it in the harness finally makes it model the spiral it was always meant to.
- **Header treatment:** an explicit "in debt — interest accruing" affordance when `balance < 0`, not merely a red number, so the self-accelerating decline is unmistakable.

items.title: Per-building profitability readout — make each building's unit economics legible
items.summary: Gameplay-clarity strand (filed 2026-06-30) — the most direct answer to 'how does the player make a profit'. Today the player sees only the corp-wide balance; they cannot tell WHICH buildings earn and which bleed. Attribute the four budget flows ([[BL-072]]) to the individual building and show its net per-tick contribution (output sales − input cost − wages − maintenance) in the Selection panel for a selected building, so siting and recipe decisions become legible at the unit level.
items.design:
**Status:** design-owed — filed from the same gameplay-clarity review as [[BL-071]] (Ben, 2026-06-30). Requires [[BL-072]] (shares its per-flow capture).

### Problem
Profit is currently legible only in aggregate (the corp balance and the trend plots). The player builds a refinery and cannot tell whether *that refinery* makes money — only that the whole corp's balance moved. This is the crux of the 'how do I make a profit' confusion: the unit economics are invisible.

### Proposed
When [[BL-072]] captures the budget flows, attribute them **per building** (each building already has wages, maintenance, and — via its recipe — input purchases and output sales). Surface the building's **net per-tick contribution** and its components in the **Selection panel** when a building is selected, and optionally a compact margin hint on the hover card. In the construction panel, an *estimated* margin for a building type at a candidate tile would close the loop with [[BL-071]] (legible placement → legible profitability), but that estimate is harder (depends on market price) — flag as a stretch.

### Open calls (Ben)
- Attribution granularity: exact per-building flows (requires threading building id through the market clear) vs a per-building **estimate** from its recipe × current market price (cheaper, approximate).
- Where it lives: Selection panel only (MVP) vs also a per-building column in the Construction Ledger.
- Whether to show realised (last tick) vs smoothed contribution.

This is the surfacing that turns the economy from 'balance goes up or down' into 'this building at this site earns X' — the strategic read the whole construction loop is meant to reward.

### Resolved (2026-06-30, Ben)
- **Attribution = estimate, not exact.** The pooled (body, resource) market commingles every building's output into the corp pool, so a sale cannot be traced back to one building without fighting the market model. Instead **estimate** per building from data already in `building_report`: output value = `output_quantity × current market price`; input cost = recipe inputs × runs × price; wages and maintenance are already computed per building in `apply_budget`. Net = value − inputs − wages − maintenance. No threading of building id through `clear_markets`.
- **Where:** the Selection panel when a building is selected (MVP) — net per-tick contribution plus its component lines (revenue / input cost / wages / maintenance). A per-building column in the Construction Ledger and a compact hover-card margin hint are stretch follow-ons.
- **Realised, not smoothed:** show the last-tick estimate. The figure is already an approximation; smoothing an estimate doubles the fuzz. The smoothed view lives at the corp level in [[BL-072]].
- **Construction-panel pre-build estimate** (margin for a type at a candidate tile, closing the loop with [[BL-071]]) stays a flagged stretch — it depends on *projecting* a market price the building has not yet sold into, which the realised readout sidesteps.

items.title: Corp × terrain viability test matrix — every generated corp has a buildable, profitable chain
items.summary: Testing strand (filed 2026-06-30): 'unit tests for different corps in different generated terrains'. A new headless harness (verifier-headless pattern) that sweeps multiple world seeds and, for each generated corporation on its assigned body, asserts a viable economic start: starting assets sit on legal terrain, the corp's industrial focus has at least one VALID placement on its body, and at least one output resource has a market — i.e. a generated corp can actually build something profitable on the terrain it was dealt. Guards against world-gen handing a corp a body where it is economically stranded.
items.design:
**Delivered 2026-07-01.** Headless harness tools/verify/corp_terrain_matrix.cpp (world-only, no SDL/Lua/ImGui): per-corp two-tier checks -- A1 asset legality + A2 buildable focus (tier-1 hard FAIL), A3 reachable market + A4 profitable chain (tier-2 WARN); exits non-zero only on a tier-1 FAIL. Canonical-world MVP (k_seed_count parameterised for a future sweep; make_hard_coded_world not yet seedable). Run: PASS -- 8 corps, 0 FAIL / 0 WARN. Findings surfaced (non-fatal): the food_rations chain is loss-making at base price (rev 48 vs cost 70, overlaps BL-078); a generated trade-corp port sits on a non-coastal tile -- passes generation can_place but would fail the player-time can_place_in_world coastal rule (a generation/player rule-consistency gap worth a follow-up). CMake target added. NOTE: promoting it into the verifier-headless skill's named list needs user OK (tool-creation-is-skill-creation).

**Status:** design-owed — filed from a gameplay-clarity review (Ben, 2026-06-30). A `world/*`-only harness, so it follows the **verifier-headless** skill (tools/verify/*.cpp over the SDL/Lua-free logic).

### Why
The generation layer (corporation + tile + nation) is deterministic but the *interaction* — does a corp's industrial focus actually fit the terrain it was placed on? — is untested. A corp generated onto a body with no valid tiles for its buildings, or no market for its outputs, is economically stranded from turn one. This is a generation-validity check, complementary to the existing `world_audit` and `construction_harness`.

### Proposed harness
For a set of seeds (sweep, not a single world), for each generated corporation:
1. **Asset legality** — every starting building/asset sits on terrain its `placement_rules` accept (no illegal authored placements).
2. **Buildable focus** — the corp's industrial focus (CORPORATION_GENERATION.md) has **≥1 valid candidate tile** on its assigned body for at least one building in that focus.
3. **Reachable market** — at least one output resource of that focus has a market centre on the body (or reachable via convoy), so production can be sold.
4. (Stretch) **Profitable chain** — a coarse check that the chain's output base_price exceeds its input + wage + maintenance cost, so the focus is not structurally loss-making on that terrain.

Report PASS/FAIL per (seed, corp) with the failing assertion named. Author the harness, then either add it to the verifier-headless skill's named list or, if skill edit is denied, run it as a one-off and note it (per CLAUDE.md § Tool creation is skill creation).

### Open calls (Ben)
- Seed set: a fixed small list (reproducible) vs a larger deterministic sweep.
- Whether assertion 4 (profitability) belongs here or is too coupled to economy tuning — could split into a separate econ-side check.
- Whether a FAIL is a hard test failure (gen bug) or a tuning warning (some bodies are *meant* to be marginal).

Serves both gameplay clarity now and the **v0.1.0 quality audit** later (generation validity is part of 'the loop is verified').

### Resolved (2026-06-30, Ben)
- **FAIL semantics = two-tier.** Assertions 1–2 (asset legality, buildable focus) are **hard FAILs** — an illegally-placed starting asset, or a focus with no valid candidate tile on its body, is a generation bug. Assertions 3–4 (reachable market, profitable chain) are **WARNs** — a body with a thin market or a marginal chain can be intended, so they surface loudly but do not break the build. The harness exits non-zero only on a tier-1 FAIL.
- **Seed set:** a fixed, small, reproducible list (≈8–16 seeds) as the MVP, with the seed count a parameter so it can widen to a deterministic sweep later without restructuring.
- **Assertion 4 stays in this harness** as a distinct, coarse profitability check (output base_price vs input + wage + maintenance), reported as a WARN — not split into a separate econ harness. It is explicitly coarse (base_price, not cleared market price); deep balance tuning is out of scope here.
- **Tooling:** a `world/*`-only harness under the **verifier-headless** skill — author `tools/verify/corp_terrain_matrix.cpp`, then add it to the skill's named list (or, if skill edit is denied, run once and note it per CLAUDE.md § Tool creation is skill creation). Serves gameplay clarity now and the v0.1.0 generation-validity audit later.

items.title: Display options window — resolution / fullscreen / vsync, persisted
items.summary: Pre-playtest QOL: the player had no way to set or remember the window size/mode. The OS window is already SDL_WINDOW_RESIZABLE (free drag-resize worked), but the startup size was hard-coded 1280x720 with no fullscreen/vsync control and nothing persisted. Adds an F10 Options window (resolution presets, fullscreen, vsync) that applies live and persists to options.cfg, plus capture of free drag-resizes. Distinct from BL-070 (in-app system menu: exit/pause) which is the session shell; this is the display-settings surface.
items.design:
**Delivered 2026-07-01 (same-session).** Scope confirmed with the developer: window + options only (no main menu / app-state machine, no save/load).

**Surface.** An ImGui Options window toggled by F10 (canvas_command::options_toggle, in the s_bindings table so it shows in the F1 cheat-sheet), modelled on the F1 help overlay. Contains a Display section: resolution combo (1280x720 / 1600x900 / 1920x1080 / 2560x1440, 'Custom' when a dragged size doesn't match), Fullscreen checkbox (borderless-desktop), VSync checkbox, a live 'Window: WxH' readout, and Close.
